back: Nuclear division producing two genetically identical nuclei with the same chromosome number as the parent nucleus.
Chromosomes condense (two chromatids visible), nucleolus disappears, spindle forms, nuclear envelope breaks down.
Spindle microtubules attach to centromeres; chromosomes line up individually on the equator.
Centromeres divide; microtubules shorten and pull sister chromatids to opposite poles.
Chromosomes reach poles and uncoil; nuclear envelopes and nucleoli reform; spindle breaks down.
Animals: cleavage furrow. Plants: cell plate from Golgi vesicles.
Number of cells in mitosis ÷ total number of cells counted.

front: Why is the root tip used for a mitosis squash?
back: The zone just behind the root cap has many dividing cells (high mitotic index).
Growth, replacement, repair, asexual reproduction and clonal expansion of lymphocytes.
